gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Gough Lui, testing against a Rohde & Schwarz NGM202 reference supply (0.05% basic accuracy), found the XTAR VX4's capacity readings ran 2–3% high, 2.78% at worst, and that the VX4 draws about 530 mW from the wall while idle with its backlight off.
standout_why: I read the four cited rival pages. 1lumen's VC4SL review (Dave, April 2022) gives measured charge current (3060 mA) and end voltage (4.19 V) but no capacity-accuracy or standby figure. Tim McMahon's VX4 review (August 2024) gives finish voltages of 4.097–4.177 V and one capacity cross-check: 6174 mAh on the VX4 against 6163 mAh on an Atorch DL24. So the rivals already cover part of the capacity-accuracy point. M0MNF's VC4SL review (April 2025) has no measurements, only the maker's current options. The manuals.plus Vapcell S4 Plus V3 page is just the manual. None of them gives a systematic capacity error measured against a lab-grade reference, or any idle power draw. HKJ's drain and termination figures for the S4+ are also missing from the rival pages, but they cover the original S4+, not the V3 that ChatGPT showed.
decides: This confirms the VX4 as a sound pick for people who want to grade 18650 cells: its capacity figures are trustworthy within 3%, leaning slightly high, so a cell that reads 2,900 mAh is really about 2,820 mAh or more. It doesn't change the order of picks. For the VC4SL, the two named measurements of end voltage, 4.19 V from 1lumen and about 4.16 V from SammysHP, both fall at or just under 4.2 V. That backs it as a charger that doesn't overcharge, at the cost of a slightly short full charge. I found no independent measurements of the Vapcell S4 Plus V3 or the Tenergy TN270, which Dealectric lists, so neither can be backed with a named number.

findings.note: Dave at 1lumen, April 2022, single cell. A 4000 mAh 21700 took 1.5 h at 3060 mA. The display was almost 0.1 V off a multimeter on some cells. This rival page is cited by ChatGPT.

findings.label: Li-ion end-of-charge voltage (SammysHP)
findings.note: SammysHP, 2021-12-03: 'Li-ion batteries were charged to about 4.16 V in my tests.' He also saw the display read 4.20 V when the real voltage was 3.9 V, and judged the IR readings 'not very accurate'.

findings.label: Termination current and drain on a cell left in the charger with power off (HKJ)
findings.value: ≈100 mA termination current; 2.2 mA Li-ion drain with power off
findings.note: HKJ (Henrik Jensen). The review is undated on the page and covers the original S4+, not the V3 that ChatGPT showed. Four cells at 3 A from 12 V drew about 4.5 A, cells reached 45–47 °C, and the heatsink 69 °C. He found the displayed internal resistance about half the actual value.
